id: title:eli-r-ph:refuse persons database models in background delete model

review.posthog_relevance: Protects ClickHouse-backed persons identity store integrity by preventing ORM deletion against the wrong database, avoiding orphaned rows or connection failures.
review.reason: Adds a database routing guard and its enforcement to prevent deleting models from the ClickHouse-backed persons database, alongside a corresponding test. This establishes a bounded correctness improvement for warehouse and identity store reliability.
review.uncertainty: Chunk does not include the full implementation of PersonDBRouter or the complete background_delete_model_task, so the exact routing mechanism and broader task behavior are not demonstrated; score relies only on the guard and its test.

observations.limitations: This chunk does not include the implementation of PersonDBRouter or the underlying database routing configuration, so the exact mechanism of how PersonDBRouter distinguishes persons-db models is not demonstrated. observations.behavior: Adds a guard function and its invocation to prevent deletion of models residing in the persons database.
observations.posthog_connection: This prevents a raw Django ORM delete from executing against a model stored in the ClickHouse-backed persons database, which could leave orphaned rows or fail due to connection routing. This protects the integrity of the ClickHouse warehouse and the person identity store.

observations.behavior: Adds a guard function implementation that checks if a model belongs to the persons database.
observations.posthog_connection: This checks the database router's classification. If the model is identified as a persons-db model, it raises an error. This establishes the enforcement point for the safety check.

observations.behavior: Adds a new test case and its setup, including the parameterized decorator and the mock for the task.
observations.posthog_connection: This tests the behavior of the command when a model is supplied that resides in the persons database. It expects the command to raise a CommandError and not invoke the deletion task, ensuring the guard is respected.
